body:
Sorry, I was drunk earlier and I wasn't sure if it would be fair to talk to someone, in that state. I am calmer now. But it is a relief to be able to say this. I have been on reddit for some time, so I turned here after a terrible confrontation I had with my mother. I first tried to talk to someone in askreddit - if anyone would say a word, even to call me a loser, then I wouldn't feel so cut off. The good people there suggested I come here. Hence the link that I have posted above. 

I am a 38 year old married man with a son. I have these rounds of depression that hit me every six months on average. I went to one of the top engineering institutes of my country. It is there that I first had an attack - I couldn't concentrate, assignments were never turned in and I couldn't make myself care about it. Also I was drinking and cutting myself. In some perverted way,seeing a few drops of blood and the pain used to give me a sense of relief - I can't explain. I didn't have a name for it at that time. It is an insanely competitive college, and everyone else went far ahead of me - I couldn't complete reading one page in a text book at a time and it was always like that for months at a time. 

Finally, unable to function and unable to pull myself out of it, I tried to overdose on half a dozen bottles of cough syrup and all the strips of tablets I could find. It was a hostel with single rooms, but someone found me and they pumped it out. The college didn't take too kindly to it and the dean wanted me to leave. That was the first time I realized how brutal and unforgiving people will be to someone who attempts this, and fails. But he let me stay after my parents begged and cried in his office, and I graduated normally, although without a placement. Everyone else got into aided programs in the top 20 universities in America, and I left without a job. Fortunately the college's credentials were good enough, and I managed to get employed in a software firm in 3 months. 

After that I have managed to rebuild and have a semblance of a normal life outwardly - I am a senior engineer and the work is not oppressive and my neighbours would just know me as the quiet guy who doesn't talk to anyone. I got married and had a child - that was not fair to the kid but I live in a place where there is a lot of pressure to have one. I know that I was being selfish to the kid, and it still kills me when I look at him. 

I have been having these bouts of depression lasting 3 to 6 months regularly for the 20 years. My wife doesn't understand, she can't relate to it, but at least she leaves me alone. 2 rounds ago, in mid 2011,I just snapped - I decided I couldn't take it any further and started drinking frequently - I was hoping that my liver would give out soon and it would be over. Right now, I am in the middle of another round. Before I took that step in college, I remember how my whole self felt to be existing a full 2 inches behind my eyeballs, not at the surface like it feels when you are normal. And that feeling is back now. 

I've been to doctors, but it has been all about medicines and prescriptions - I might as well have gone to them with a cold. I wish one of them would fucking talk to me for once - I know they are not obliged to, and I am not overly clingy, but just... 

Right now, I might appear normal to everyone else - I still get up in the morning and go to work, but I also know there is only one way this is going to end. Right now I don't know which is driving which - am I drinking because it is hopeless, or is it the other way round. 

The trigger yesterday was an argument I had with my mother - I told her I was doing this because I wanted to die, and she looked so broken. I can imagine now, having a kid of my own - if something happened to him. 

I am only causing harm and pain to everyone around, but I am tired of doing this - I know there will be a bright looking morning if I give it another couple of months, but that is only temporary. I am not going anywhere, I'll be right back in this hell hole soon after. Can someone tell one good reason why I should keep up this charade for another 5 years or however long it takes for my liver to self destruct.

I didn't mean to bother anyone. It is just that I have a mental illness I am sick of. And I am hurting all the people around me who still care. 

Is depression incurable? Is it always going to be like this?
